top_signals.title: Oil Tops $100 on Supply Fears,  Apple Faces a Big Test
top_signals.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn and Bailey Lipschultz on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Scott Bessent turns up the heat on global markets, from the yen to Treasuries. Brent crude breaks above $100 as fresh Middle East attacks stoke supply fears. Apple faces sky-high expectations ahead of its biggest event in years. Plus, Vale CFO Marcelo Bacci on resilient iron ore demand, and Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon exits with a stark warning over AI risk. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Oil Prices Reach Six-Week High
top_signals.summary: Oil prices rose to a six-week high on Tuesday after Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen attacked Saudi energy facilities, setting oil installations ablaze and threatening a major expansion of the six-month-old Middle East war.Brent crude futures rose 70 cents, or 0.7%, to $97.70 a barrel at 10:56 a.m.

top_signals.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
top_signals.summary: A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.
